lastRun.sentence: J'ai rendez-vous ___ le dentiste demain matin.
lastRun.sentenceNl: Ik heb morgenochtend een afspraak bij de tandarts.
lastRun.why: 'chez' is used before a person or practitioner (the dentist), whereas 'à' would need a place or institution.
lastRun.note: chez is at or to a person's home or practice (chez le médecin); à is at or to a place or institution (à l'école).

lastRun.sentence: Il a plu toute la ___ sans s'arrêter.
lastRun.sentenceNl: Het heeft de hele dag door geregend.
lastRun.why: The expression 'toute la journée' stresses the whole span of the day, requiring 'journée'.
lastRun.note: jour for a plain count or a point in time; journée when the span of the day is felt (toute la journée).

lastRun.sentenceNl: We zien elkaar wel een andere dag.
lastRun.why: 'un autre jour' refers to a point in time, so 'jour' fits, not the duration-focused 'journée'.
lastRun.note: jour for a plain count or a point in time; journée when the span of the day is felt (toute la journée).

lastRun.sentence: Cet été, nous allons ___ le musée du Louvre.
lastRun.sentenceNl: Deze zomer gaan we het Louvre bezoeken.
lastRun.why: The object is a place (a museum), so 'visiter' is correct; 'rendre visite à' is only for people.
lastRun.note: visiter is for a place; rendre visite à is for a person.

lastRun.sentence: Ce week-end, je vais ___ les enfants à la mer.
lastRun.sentenceNl: Dit weekend neem ik de kinderen mee naar zee.
lastRun.why: The children are taken away to another place (the sea), so 'emmener' fits, not 'amener'.
lastRun.note: amener brings a person or animal toward the point of reference; emmener takes them away from it.
